findings.title: The install-command rule rejects a sentence-ending period that the token rule accepts
findings.recommendation: Make the install-command boundary the token rule's own: replace the lookahead (?![A-Za-z0-9.]) with (?![A-Za-z0-9]|\.\d), so a prose install command that ends a sentence still counts, while #v2.0.10 and #v2.0.1.5 stay rejected. Add one fixture line to the 'A page without its install command fails' test showing a sentence-ending command passes.
findings.reproduction: node probe of the shipped regex against 'Run npm install -g github:las-sal/orbit-spec#v2.0.1.' returns false (the page would be reported as carrying no install command), while the token rule reports the same v2.0.1 as current; with (?![A-Za-z0-9]|\.\d) it returns true, and '#v2.0.10' / '#v2.0.1.5' still return false. The shipped docs carry the command in code fences, so nothing fails today.

findings.title: The 2.0.1 entry's kept-names list omits the OPENSPEC:START/END markers a user sees in their files
findings.recommendation: Either add the rc-file and instruction-file markers (OPENSPEC:START / OPENSPEC:END, written by src/core/config.ts and the bash/zsh completion installers) to the bullet's list, so it matches CLAUDE.md's kept set for what a user can see, or leave it: the bullet says 'Some names are kept', which does not claim completeness.

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: Add the OPENSPEC:START / OPENSPEC:END markers to the CHANGELOG bullet's kept-names list.

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Leave the bullet as is; 'Some names' already signals the list is partial.

commentary: Probed hardest at the new version check, since it is the only logic the change adds. The token regex holds on the edge cases the spec names (fourth component, letter or dot before, letter after, sentence-ending period, 2.0.10 versus 2.0.1), the phrase admission is file-scoped and wrap-tolerant, an install target never takes a value admission, and the stale-admission rule keys on object identity of the admissions, which works because admittedBy carries the same objects. The shipped-docs test runs over docSurfaces(), which excludes the pending-rewrite list (empty today), matching the MODIFIED requirement's whole-docs clause. Pass 0 was done inline rather than by invoking orbit-verify: all 10 tasks checked, the seven new scenarios each carry an @scenario behaviour declaration in test/core/user-docs/version.test.ts, the four carried scenarios of the MODIFIED block are declared in pending-rewrite.test.ts, orbit validate release is valid, and orbit fingerprint --check reports the carried block verified. From the live checkout (HEAD 49a44e1b, the pair launch commit): npm run build plus npm test give 177 test files and 3747 tests passing, and node bin/orbit.js --version prints 2.0.1. Every remaining 2.0.0 in the tree is history (architecture docs, archived emits, test comments about the landing-page stage, the CHANGELOG's own 2.0.0 entry) or the admitted README phrase. Pass 6 ran as a targeted drift sweep (version residue across src, test and docs; orbit validate --sources and --all --strict; the CHANGELOG against CLAUDE.md's kept-names set), not as a full four-category audit-drift invocation. Passes 4 and 5 were skipped because orbit/lenses/ does not exist.

direction.reasoning:
The change does what its stage asks of the repository: the bump, the CHANGELOG entry, the five doc sites and a check that will catch the next bump the docs miss, all with tests shown able to fail and a green full suite.
Both findings are polish. Neither affects the shipped docs or the release path, so either can be taken in a walk or left.
The stage's real exit (G4: an install from the pushed tag prints 2.0.1 and init says orbit) lies after merge and is graded at ratification, as the design states; nothing in this diff stands in its way.
